clue.text: In this part of racetrack bet on five consecutive cards

parts.note: to back a horse or team is to bet on it
in poker a straight is a hand of five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: A punter places a poker-style wager at one stretch of the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this' only links the definition to the wordplay. The back straight is the straight section of a racetrack on the far side from the finishing post.
explanation.definitionFit: On an oval track the stretch opposite the home run past the stands is its far straight.

clue.text: Sat awkwardly on lift with legs apart

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means doing it clumsily, so the letters of 'Sat' are jumbled

parts.note: a lift is a ride given in someone's car

explanation.surface: Someone perches clumsily on a lift, legs splayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges SAT into AST; 'on' joins it to RIDE in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on either side of something is sitting straddled.

clue.text: Hold on to rice wine memento

parts.note: to hold on to something is to keep it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone saves a bottle of rice wine as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir kept to remind one of a person or event is a memento.

clue.text: An international trial

explanation.surface: A player is given a trial for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international cricket or rugby match, and a test is also any trial or examination.

clue.text: Each run out, getting less than versatile cricketer

parts.note: 'all' can mean each, as in 'two all'
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket
under means less than, as in 'under ten pounds'

explanation.surface: Every run-out makes a team look less than a side of versatile players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' only joins the pieces. In cricket an all-rounder is a player good at both batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: A player useful with both bat and ball is the versatile type cricket prizes.

clue.text: Guarantee initially covers same arrangement for athletics meeting

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece covering another sits on top of it, so G comes first
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of 'Guarantee' is used
an arrangement of the word 'same' means its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A guarantee covers the same arrangements for a sports meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns SAME into AMES, and 'covers' puts G above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commonwealth Games and Highland games are athletics meetings.

clue.text: Fabulous creature takes work as prostitute

parts.note: a troll is a creature from fables and folk tales
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: A mythical beast takes up sex work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable here, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is an old insulting word for a promiscuous woman or a whore.

clue.text: Caving in Sweden was hot to start with and full of adventure

indicators.note: these words place the Sweden-was-hot pieces at the start, before the caving-in piece

parts.note: S is the international vehicle registration code for Sweden
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
caving in means buckling, collapsing under pressure

explanation.surface: A Swedish cave collapsed in the heat, which made for an adventurous trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caving in' suggests potholing but means collapsing; 'to start with' puts the Sweden, was and hot pieces ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes daring, swaggering adventure such as pirate films.

clue.text: Under decent PE, suitably organised, it's unheard of

indicators.note: letters suitably organised are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Sports lessons run decently and properly would be a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suitably organised' rearranges all thirteen letters of UNDER DECENT PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any earlier example is unheard of.

clue.text: Part of horse's back droops

explanation.surface: A horse's back sags.
explanation.definitionFit: The withers are the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades, and a plant that withers wilts and sags.

clue.text: Left a sitting member with nothing on to take off

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, the sitting member for a seat
O is the round figure for zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sitting MP left with nothing on is ripe for mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' means mimic, not remove clothes, though the surface's naked MP pulls that way.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them; satirising them in writing is the same mockery.

clue.text: Petticoats and bloomers

explanation.surface: A list of women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are undergarments like petticoats, and slips are also blunders, which is the slang sense of bloomers.

clue.text: Coal runs out according to state official

definitions.note: consular is the adjective of a noun for a state official; the definition stands loosely for it

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of 'Coal runs' are out of order

explanation.surface: A government official reports that the coal has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COAL RUNS; 'according to' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a government official posted abroad, and consular means relating to that office.

clue.text: Rosie tries cooking in specialist restaurant

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or altering, so the letters of 'Rosie tries' are changed

explanation.surface: Rosie has a go at cooking in a specialist restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks literal but rearranges ROSIE TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in meat roasted on a turning spit.

clue.text: Smash to indicate position of game: at Wimbledon it's critical

definitions.text: position of game: at Wimbledon it's critical

parts.note: to smash something is to break it
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator says a smash marks a crucial point in a Wimbledon match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash' looks like the tennis shot. Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship; in tennis a break point lets the receiver win the opponent's service game.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the stage where the receiver can win the server's game is a crucial position.

clue.text: Heroic tale taken from the Pictish Chronicles

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tale of heroes is drawn from the ancient Pictish chronicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'thE PICtish'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative of heroic deeds.

clue.text: Kiss rep perhaps after a period of relaxation in winter resort

definitions.text: period of relaxation in winter resort

indicators.note: after places the scrambled piece behind the letter A
perhaps suggests the word 'Kiss rep' may take another form, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A holiday rep might get a kiss when the day's skiing is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges KISS REP into PRESSKI, and 'after' puts it behind A.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising and unwinding at a ski resort when the day on the slopes ends.

clue.text: Bottle stopped by this Irish town

explanation.surface: A bottle is corked in an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork stoppers a bottle, and Cork is a city and county in the south of Ireland.

clue.text: Went up with trendy fruit from flowering shrub

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, went up
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable plant's fruit has gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed-pod left after a wild rose flowers is a hip, a fruit of the bush.

clue.text: Extra for cricket broadcast is common

parts.note: a wide is a bowled ball out of the batter's reach, scored as an extra run
broadcast means scattered or spread about

explanation.surface: Cricket extras are shown on ordinary TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests television but means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found over a large area is prevalent, that is common.

clue.text: Officer commanding work unit with the French put up with Spanish painter

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
the erg is a unit of work in physics
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A commanding officer and the French team put up with a Spanish artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns OC, ERG and LE, written in that order, into one backward run. El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Toledo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Toledo master known as 'the Greek' is the famous artist of Spain's Golden Age.

clue.text: Heavy drinker has a point -it's a luxuriant state

parts.note: a lush is slang for a drunkard
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness's neighbours like Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A drunk makes a fair point in a rich setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins the pieces; 'point' is a headland, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lush, thick and abundant in growth, is the condition of luxuriance.

clue.text: Pinch half an inch and cut in

parts.note: to nip is to pinch

indicators.note: half an signals that only the first half of the word 'inch' is used

explanation.surface: Someone trims half an inch with a pinch and a snip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half an' takes IN from INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip in is to push in quickly, as a driver does when cutting in.

clue.text: The Spanish spirit in NE Scotland

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a town found in NE Scotland

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Spaniard drinks gin in the north-east of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place clause: Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin, a cathedral town in Moray, is a place located in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Reckless collision — starter's gone

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, and it has gone, so it is dropped

parts.note: a crash is a collision

explanation.surface: A careless crash leaves a race without its starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter's gone' drops the C from CRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash act is impetuous and done without thought.

clue.text: Japanese drama and most of musical drama is a failure

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked theatre

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an opera is a musical drama

explanation.surface: A mash-up of Japanese theatre and opera is a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' takes OPER from OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success is a hopeless case, a failure.

clue.text: A third of autumn trees damaged: it's grave

indicators.note: a third of the six-letter word autumn is its first two letters
damaged means broken up, so the letters of 'trees' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A third of the autumn trees are damaged, which is serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of' takes AU from AUTUMN; 'damaged' turns TREES into STERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and austere both describe a stern, solemn manner.

clue.text: Furniture removal van parking in front of church with new religious painting

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
ante is Latin for before, in front of
an icon is a religious painting of the Eastern Church

explanation.surface: A removal lorry is parked outside a church with a new icon inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' looks like a placing instruction but supplies ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantechnicon is a large van used to move house contents.
